Hi Alex / team — following up with the technical details we discussed. I summarized recommended approaches below and included a short SDK snippet and links to an internal setup steps file (sdk_setup_steps.txt).

Auth & SDK:
- Recommendation: Start POC with scoped API keys for speed; switch to OIDC (short-lived tokens) for prod. Redwood supports both. For OIDC we integrate with Azure AD / Okta and can accept JWTs with an audience claim.
- KMS: We support using your KMS for key wrapping in Dedicated/Private.

Example (NodeJS) — SDK init + OIDC token header (pseudo):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({
  endpoint: 'https://api.redwood.ai',
  auth: { type: 'oidc', token: process.env.OIDC_TOKEN }
});

// Structured output + tool-calling example (function calling style)
const resp = await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-chat-13b',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are ACME support assistant. Follow strict action schema.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Refund request for order #12345' }
  ],
  tools: [ 'order_lookup', 'create_refund' ],
  output_schema: { type: 'object', properties: { action: { type: 'string' }, details: { type: 'object' } } }
});

Routing & latency/cost controls:
- Tag routes by traffic type (agent_ui vs async_batch) and route to smaller/faster model families accordingly.
- Use prefix caching for common prompts and KV cache reuse to reduce per-token cost.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Option A (recommended): Generate ACME embeddings via Redwood and store vectors in your Elastic cluster. We provide batched embedding APIs and a reranker endpoint that takes candidate IDs + query to return ranked list.
- Option B: Continue producing embeddings in your pipeline; use Redwood only for reranking/generation.

Prompt versioning & governance:
- Prompt templates: store canonical templates in a git-backed prompt repo. Redwood can record prompt metadata (version tag, author, checksum) as part of each request metadata.
- Immutable history: we recommend storing a checksum + pointer to the repo commit for every system prompt used in a rollout.
- Prompt-injection mitigations: multilayer approach — input sanitization, strict system prompts, model-side safety filters, and automated tests (see below).

Red-team & testing:
- We run a red-team engagement style: (1) baseline injection fuzzing, (2) domain-specific adversarial cases, (3) regression tests per prompt change. We can provide a red-team report template and run the first pass jointly.

Attachments: sdk_setup_steps.txt (step-by-step), red_team_report_v1.pdf (example).

Let me know if you want a shortened checklist for your security team; I can convert the above into a one-pager. Also confirm the deep-dive time — I’ll prepare a short demo showing embeddings -> reranker -> structured tool call.
